ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute with no change to the fare; no voucher issued. Optionally note the driver's two prior upheld no-show disputes for routine account monitoring (profile fact only, not this ruling).
ruling.reasoning:
Cancellation was by the driver on a rider-no-show basis, so the fee can only stand through NS-0 and NS-1 [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles NS-1(i) and (ii): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 and was 41 m from the pickup at that moment, within the 200 m radius, corroborated by the closest approach of 35 m [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) is settled by the trace: from the 17:19:15 tap until the 17:22:55 cancellation the driver stayed continuously inside the radius for 220 s (3 min 40 s), exceeding the 180 s (>) default bar, and the wait trace has no hole between arrival confirmation and cancellation [F6][F4][F2][NS-1].

The records also show a longer presence than the minimum: the platform recorded arrival at 17:17:50, the driver was inside 200 m cumulatively 5 min 5 s before cancelling, and the car was stationary 4 min 5 s at 54 m from the pickup up to the cancellation [F5][F2][F3][NS-1]. Whether the clock runs from the tap or from the platform arrival, the qualifying wait is met, so the 40-second margin the rider attacks does not remove the fee [F4][F6][NS-1].

The rider's complaint that she "came out a minute after" the cancellation is a statement with no system corroboration: no GPS, timeline or chat record shows her present or boarding during the wait, and the chat contains only the driver's two timestamped messages [F11][F9][F10]. System records override statements, and there is nothing here supporting the rider's account [F2][F3][NS-1].

The driver's written statement that he waited over 3 minutes before cancelling is consistent with, not contrary to, these records, and is not needed to establish the elements [F12][NS-1]. Accordingly NS-1 is satisfied on all three elements, the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee is validly earned, and no refund arises [F7][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 (refund_full) is not triggered and no flag_account follows from this case [NS-2].

The driver's profile (3 disputes, 2 upheld in the no-show category) cannot decide this case; it is only a possible basis for an added account action where the case is established against the driver (RD-6), which it is not here [F17][RD-6]. Rider profile facts likewise do not decide it [F16][RD-6]. The dispute was filed within the 30-day window, but NS-7 concerns how an upheld refund is paid and does not create one [F4][F7][NS-7]. No traffic records exist for the window, which is immaterial to a no-show case [F13][F14].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement in context — the chat is a plain arrival notice and a cancellation notice, and the driver's statement is a routine no-show account; no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears [F9][F10][F12]. Safety concern: none.

rejected_claims.reason: Conceded and correct on element (ii), but the claim that the outcome 'turns on element (iii)' does not help the rider: NS-1(iii) is satisfied — 220 s of continuous waiting after the 17:19:15 tap exceeds the 180 s bar [F6][F4][NS-1].
The rider's own claim establishes the driver's case: 17:19:15 to 17:22:55 is 3 min 40 s of continuous waiting inside the radius, exceeding the >3 min requirement in NS-1(iii) [F6][F4][NS-1].

Counting from the driver's own tap is exactly what NS-1(iii) prescribes; the 17:22 message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' reports completion of the measure taken from the tap, it does not disprove it [F10][F6][NS-1].

Absence of a record showing the rider unreachable does not defeat NS-1, whose elements are arrival confirmation, proximity and continuous waiting; those are met by the system records [F2][F3][F6][NS-1].
The driver's statement F12 is consistent with the system records F2, F3, F5 and F6, so it is not outweighed by them, and the elements are established from the records alone [F12][F6][NS-1].

Since NS-1 is satisfied, the fee is validly earned, NS-2 refund_full does not arise, and the profile fact of 2 prior upheld no-show disputes cannot decide this case or trigger flag_account; RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver [F17][F6][F4][NS-2][RD-6].
No refund of the $6.61 arises because the fee was validly incurred under NS-1; FARE-1 does not apply to a no-show cancellation fee of the correct published amount [F7][F4][NS-1].
The 30-day filing window and voucher form of payment under NS-7 govern how an upheld refund would be issued; they do not create an entitlement where the fee was earned [F4][F7][NS-7].
The chat is complete and timestamped, but completeness alone does not resolve the rider's arrival; the elements of NS-1 are instead established by the GPS/timeline records [F11][F2][F6][NS-1].

The driver's profile cannot decide the case and, since the case is not established against the driver, RD-6's condition (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) is unmet, so no account action follows [F17][F6][RD-6].
